Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg. EDSA corner Mapagmahal Street, Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE MR. ORLANDO L. DE GUZMAN Sangguniang Bayan Member Municipality of Bustos Province of Bulacan PROVINCIAL DIRECTOR MYRA B. MORAL Office of the Provincial Director Capitol Compound, Malolos City Bulacan DILG OPINION NO. 147 S. 2010 NOV 2010 Dear SB Member De Guzman/ Provincial Director Moral: This has reference to your respective letters seeking clarification on the propriety and legality of approving municipal development plan resolutions despite the questionable representation of the non-governmental organizations (NGO) in the Local Development Council (LDC) and proffering the following queries, to wit: a. Whether or not the composition of the LDC is technically compliant with the provisions of the 1991 LGC taking into account the questionable representation of the NGOs; b. Whether or not the resolutions approved by the LDC are valid; and c. Whether or not it is appropriate for the SB to adopt the said LDC resolutions. In reply to your first query, may we point out that the LDC may convene provided that it meets the quorum requirement under Section 110 of the LGC. Since the number of members of the LDC to constitute a quorum is not provided under said Section, then a simple majority of the membership of the LDC shall constitute a quorum to transact official business. Quorum as defined in the case of Manuel Zamora vs. Gov. Jose Caballero, et. al., (G.R. No. 147767. January 14, 2002), is the "number of members of a body which, when legally assembled, will enable the body to transact its proper business or that number which makes a lawful body and gives it power to pass upon a law or ordinance or do any valid act." When required to constitute a quorum, "majority" means the number greater than half or more than half of the total. Hence, notwithstanding the questionable representation of the NGOs present during said meeting, the LDC may convene and transact official business provided it meets the quorum requirement.

Anent the second and third query, may we direct the DILG Provincial Office's attention to Memorandum No. 2010-01 and Memorandum Order No. 2010-02. Under said Memoranda, referrals to the DILG Central Office shall only be made if the issue or controversy involved entail difficult question of law which necessitate the issuance of new Department policy guidelines. In addition, the queries proffered involved questions on presumptively valid acts that already enjoy the presumption of regularity on the part of the public officer concerned, hence shall not be addressed by this Office. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. cc: L S.08:rb Very truly yours, ATTY. JES B. DOQUE IV Director Ill VICE MAYOR LEONIDA L. RIVERA Municipality of Bustos, Bulacan OSEC.De Guzman.doc
